title: How To Create A Custom Avatar In Avatar Editor
description: In this tutorial, we’ll walk you through creating a customized avatar using the Avatar Editor feature.
transcript: Hello, welcome to the Clo tutorial. In this tutorial, we'll walk you through creating a customized avatar using the Avatar Editor feature. First, load the default female avatar from the Clo Library Avatar folder. Then click Avatar in the main menu bar and select Avatar Editor to open the window. The size chart is at the bottom of the window. We will start by inputting the width and height measurements. We continue with under bust, 28 and total height, 66. As you can see, once these values are input, the circumference, height, and length values below are automatically adjusted. This is because Clo uses algorithm-based data to find the most natural body shape based on the width and height we've just entered. Let's also enter the inseam value to create a more accurate body shape. Next, click on the show all measurements icon. It will display all the deactivated items. Now let's start with the items under the height category. The automatically populated bust height is already quite common. This means the algorithm-based data is effectively reflecting the body shape of a real human figure. You can activate the measurement and input your value if you need more detailed adjustments. Here as the difference is in the tolerance, we will leave it as it is. Let's move on to the next items. The under bust value is also in the tolerance range. Therefore you may choose to activate and adjust the value or leave it as is. Next is waist height. Here you can see a difference compared to the size chart, about an inch or more. In this case the size needs to be adjusted. To do so, it is recommended to first adjust the measure line to match the chart. Then activate and enter your measurement. To adjust the measure line, we use the edit measure tool. Then click on the waist measure line and drag it downward. As you do this, you'll notice that the waist height value in the avatar editor adjusts accordingly. Try to match it with the value in the size chart. Next, we compare the measurement value. Once again, if the algorithm generated value is within the tolerance range, you can keep it. Otherwise, you can always apply the exact value from the chart. Just like with the waist, you can also adjust the measure lines of high hip and low hip. If there's a slight discrepancy between the chart and the current values, simply drag the lines to align them with the size chart. Once you've finished adjusting the height related items, let's now move to set details to activate specific measurement fields. Here in the checkbox list, you can select the size items you wish to enter manually. One thing to note is that the center back neck to wrist value under length is calculated by adding the arm length and half of the across shoulder center back neck values. Therefore, instead of entering all three values, we recommend entering either the value of center back neck to wrist or arm length and across shoulder center back neck. Once done, close the window. Now complete the avatar by entering the values of the center back neck to wrist value and across shoulder center back neck. We hope that this tutorial helps you building your own avatar with your size chart. Thanks for watching.
markdown_content: ## Overview of Creating a Custom Avatar Using Avatar Editor This section explains the process of creating a customized avatar in Clo's Avatar Editor, focusing on inputting body measurements, understanding algorithm-based adjustments, and customizing measurement lines to match a size chart. Key terms include Avatar Editor, size chart, algorithm-based data, measurement lines, and tolerance range. ## Loading the Default Avatar and Opening Avatar Editor Start by loading the default female avatar from the Clo Library Avatar folder. Then, access the Avatar Editor by clicking **Avatar** in the main menu bar and selecting **Avatar Editor**. The size chart is displayed at the bottom of the editor window, serving as a reference for inputting measurements. ## Inputting Base Measurements and Algorithm-Based Adjustments Begin by entering key measurements such as width, height, under bust (e.g., 28 inches), and total height (e.g., 66 inches). Once these values are input, related circumference, height, and length parameters adjust automatically. This auto-adjustment uses Clo's algorithm-based data, which calculates the most natural body shape based on the initial inputs. Adding the inseam measurement further refines the body shape accuracy. ## Reviewing and Adjusting Measurements Click the **Show All Measurements** icon to reveal all measurement items, including deactivated ones. Focus first on the height-related measurements: - **Bust Height**: Usually auto-populated and typically matches common human proportions, reflecting effective algorithm modeling. - **Under Bust**: Usually within acceptable tolerance; activation and manual adjustment are optional. - **Waist Height**: If there is a notable discrepancy (e.g., over an inch) compared to the size chart, adjustment is needed. ### Adjusting Measurement Lines for Accuracy To adjust measurements like waist height: 1. Use the **Edit Measure Tool**. 2. Click and drag the waist measurement line downward to better align with the size chart. 3. Observe how the waist height value in the Avatar Editor updates dynamically. Repeat similar adjustments for **high hip** and **low hip** measurement lines if discrepancies exist. Align all measurement lines as closely as possible with the size chart to ensure avatar accuracy. After adjusting, compare the updated measurements with the size chart. If the algorithm-generated values fall within the tolerance range, manual changes can be skipped. Otherwise, activate and input the precise values from the size chart. ## Activating and Entering Specific Measurement Fields In the **Set Details** section, use the checkbox list to activate specific measurement fields you want to enter manually. Note the following important relationship between measurements under the length category: - The **Center Back Neck to Wrist** measurement is calculated as the sum of **Arm Length** plus half of the **Across Shoulder Center Back Neck** value. - To avoid redundancy, enter either the **Center Back Neck to Wrist** value alone or both the **Arm Length** and **Across Shoulder Center Back Neck** values. Once all desired measurements are entered and adjusted, close the window to finalize the avatar. ## Finalizing the Custom Avatar Complete the avatar creation by confirming the values for **Center Back Neck to Wrist** and **Across Shoulder Center Back Neck**. The Avatar Editor now reflects a customized avatar that corresponds accurately to the provided size chart, thanks to precise input, measurement line adjustments, and Clo's algorithmic body shape calculations.
